dedupe_keys.name: costs of illness in the 1993 waterborne cryptosporidium outbreak milwaukee wisconsin

description: This journal article estimates the economic cost of the 1993 Milwaukee waterborne cryptosporidiosis outbreak, in which an estimated 403,000 residents of an area of about 1.61 million became ill after an ineffective filtration process failed to remove Cryptosporidium oocysts at a water treatment plant. Using data from 11 greater Milwaukee hospitals and outbreak epidemiology, the authors put the total cost at 96.2 million dollars, made up of 31.7 million in medical costs and 64.6 million in lost productivity, with average costs of 116 dollars for mild, 475 for moderate and 7,808 for severe illness. They argue that such costs should count in decisions about public drinking water safety. Coverage: one outbreak, with tables of cost by illness severity. Access: a free article; the licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: the study is retrospective and covers illness costs, not the later treatment upgrades. It supports risk-cost and treatment investment appraisal for water safety, and relates to the Flint water crisis case study in the catalogue.
